title: Token runway & FastPath evaluation - Cascade Ventures
summary: Initial discovery to map token runway, tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and experiment (FastPath) for batching and KV caching. Discussed baseline per-token targets, security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), pilot timeline and benchmarking plan.
topics: per-token pricing and target unit economics
batching strategies and kv/prefix cache impact
hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
pilot scope, benchmarks, and next-step deliverables

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-20
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Anand (Cascade CTO), Marcus Liu (Infra), Elena Gomez (PM)

Summary (auto-gen): token runway, FastPath eval, security checklist, pilot scope, send cost model

[00:00] Jenna Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jenna, AE on the account. Marco from our SE team is with me. Quick intro round?
[00:12] Priya Anand: Hi, I'm Priya, CTO at Cascade. We build a marketplace recommender and are looking at adding conversational assistants and summarization. We're here to understand cost & hosting options.
[00:22] Marcus Liu: Marcus, infra. Focused on ops, SLOs, and where data needs to live — we've got residency constraints for EU and some PII paths.
[00:30] Elena Gomez: Elena, product. We care about latency for user-facing flows and a sensible token runway for Q4.
[00:38] Marco Diaz: Great. Quick note on goal — we want to map per-token economics for typical flows, show where batching and prefix/K V cache helps, and propose a pilot (FastPath) to quantify real burn.
[00:50] Priya: "Prefix/K V cache"? can you explain what that is, sorry transcription sometimes?
[00:55] Marco Diaz: Sure, yep. We do prefix caching — basically when prompts share common prefix or context we cache KV cache entries so the model doesn't recompute tokens from scratch; that's the K V cache. It dramatically cuts per-token compute for multi-turn dialogs.
[01:10] Marcus: That sounds... promising. Our current spike pattern is chatty during daytime, like 10x more than off hours. Need to understand batching latency tradeoff.
[01:20] Jenna: Exactly. We'll cover batching windows, continuous batching vs immediate paths. For Hosted, you get Smart batching on our side; Dedicated gives you more control and lower marginal cost at scale; Private gives residency and full control but higher ops baseline.

--- Topics: Per-token economics ---
[02:05] Elena: What are realistic per-token numbers we should plan for? We have a budget of about $150k net new for inference for Q4.
[02:14] Jenna: With Redwood Hosted on a mid-size open model, ballpark generation tokens can be $0.0006 to $0.002 per token depending on model and length. But the levers change that: batching, quantization, caching, and model choice.
[02:32] Priya: So that range is wide. Our use case is short dialogs, avg response 80 tokens, sometimes multi-turn ~6 turns.
[02:40] Marco: For that profile, batching helps less because responses are short and latency matters. However KV cache helps across turns — if you have repeated context across 6 turns, you can reduce compute by ~20-40% depending on hit rate.
[02:54] Marcus: Is that 20-40 real world? What assumptions?
[02:57] Marco: Assumes a 30-50% cache hit on prefixes and typical seq length distribution. We'll need your sample prompts to simulate. We'll also try dynamic batching where small windows (10–30ms) collect requests without adding user-visible latency in many cases.

[03:20] Jenna: Also quantization profiles: 8-bit int vs 4-bit quant can save throughput costs but sometimes affects quality. We'll propose specific quantized variants during the pilot.

--- Security & Residency ---
[03:45] Priya: SOC2 + SSO are must-haves, and data-at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS for Private. What do you support?
[03:52] Jenna: Hosted: SOC2, TLS in transit, optional field-level redaction, but for CMK/KMS you need Dedicated with customer-managed keys or Private where you control the KMS. We support SAML SSO and RBAC for role separation.
[04:06] Marcus: Audit logs? We need immutability and long retention for certain flows.
[04:10] Marco: We have request-level audit logs in Redwood Console; retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has shorter retention tiers unless you add the compliance package.

[04:35] Elena: If we go Dedicated, does that mean single-tenant GPUs? What's the ramp and SLA?
[04:40] Jenna: Dedicated is reserved capacity with pinned GPU pools; SLA-backed p99 latency and throughput targets based on commit. Ramp depends on region and quota but we typically can provision initial capacity in 2–4 weeks for standard pools. Private on-prem is longer.

--- Cost modeling exchange ---
[05:10] Priya: Walk me through what you mean by "token runway". We want to understand how long $150k will last under expected growth.
[05:18] Marco: Token runway = budget / (tokens per month). We'll simulate multiple scenarios: conservative (higher per-token cost, lower caching), optimistic (good caching + batching), and growth curve. For short dialogs the key is tokens per end-user session * daily active users.
[05:33] Priya: Our current estimate: 30k daily active users, avg 3 sessions, 120 tokens generated per session => ~10.8M tokens/day. That seems high.
[05:44] Jenna: At 10.8M/day, multiply by 30 gives ~324M tokens/month. At $0.0006/token that's ~$194k/mo — so monthly, not runway. With caching and model adjustments you could push it down but it shows the sensitivity.
[06:02] Elena: Right that's why we need to tune model size and fallback strategies.

--- Tradeoffs & Fallbacks ---
[06:20] Marcus: Can Redwood do model routing? Like route low-priority requests to a smaller model automatically?
[06:24] Marco: Yes — routing policies by latency/cost/priority. You can route the majority of safe generation to a cheaper quantized variant and reserve the high-quality large model for critical flows. That reduces per-token effective cost.
[06:37] Priya: What's the overhead of routing? Any extra latency?
[06:40] Marco: Negligible if models are warmed. Warm start costs exist, but we can keep warmed pools for hot paths. Warmed models do carry baseline cost in Dedicated.

[07:00] Jenna: Also important: caching is orthogonal to model choice — a smaller model with high cache hits can be cheaper than a big model with no cache. We'll simulate both.

--- Pilot / FastPath plan ---
[07:20] Jenna: Proposed FastPath pilot: 4–8 weeks. Week 0-1: data ingest + perf simulation; Week 2-3: hosted baseline run; Week 4: Dedicated capacity trial (if wanted) + cost model; Week 5-6: results + recommendations.
[07:36] Priya: We prefer an 8-week pilot because we have weekly usage variance, and want weekend/weekday differences.
[07:42] Jenna: Sounds good. We'll scope for 8.

[08:00] Marco: For the pilot we'll need: sample prompt set, traffic distribution, and 7-day logs if possible for realistic warm/cold behavior. We'll produce a checklist.
[08:10] Priya: We'll extract logs, though some may have PII. Can you handle partial redaction?
[08:14] Marco: Yes, redactable fields are fine for simulation but we prefer realistic tokens. If necessary we can run a shadow run inside your VPC for Private/Dedicated to avoid sending PII to hosted systems.

[08:30] Marcus: About pricing — do you provide committed discounts for Dedicated?
[08:34] Jenna: Yes, reserved commitments reduce per-token compute pricing. We'll share a sliding scale: 3-month / 12-month commits with graduated discounts and burst capacity options.

--- Questions from Cascade ---
[09:05] Elena: How do you measure cache hit rates and how transparent is that in console?
[09:10] Marco: Console shows cache hit/miss metrics per route and per model; you can export time-series. We also show token-level cost breakdown including cached vs generated tokens.
[09:22] Priya: What about SLOs if we route to fallback models? Do you allow automatic fallback if the primary model exceeds latency?
[09:28] Marco: Yes, Smart routing supports fallback policies — e.g., if p99 > threshold, fall back to smaller model. There's also auto-graceful-degrade so you can trade quality for latency.

--- Realistic example run-through ---
[10:00] Marco: Let's do a quick calc example — hypothetical: 100k sessions/day, avg 3 replies/session of 80 tokens = 24M tokens/day. If you route 70% to small model at $0.0003/token and 30% to large at $0.001/token, blended rate = 0.00048/token. That equates to ~11.5k/day dollars? sorry badly spoken — math: 24M * 0.00048 = $11,520/day => ~345k/mo.
[10:30] Priya: That's still outside our $150k Q4 bucket. So we'd need heavy caching, user surface restrictions, or commit to Dedicated to lower it.

[10:50] Jenna: Also consider per-call trimming — you can truncate context, do retrieval-augmented summarization at shorter lengths, or move some flows to embeddings for reranking vs full generation.

--- Compliance details ---
[12:05] Marcus: For Private on-prem: what's the install artifact and support model?
[12:10] Marco: Private comes as a control-plane that can run in your VPC and optionally an on-prem worker bundle for air-gapped environments. We support KMS/HSM integrations and will provide runbooks and 24/7 enterprise support for Private contracts.
[12:24] Priya: Do you have HIPAA / specific healthcare compliance?
[12:28] Jenna: We have SOC2 Type II; HIPAA needs a tailored Business Associate Addendum — we can discuss legal. Private deployments make HIPAA compliance easier.

--- Misc transcription noise / interruption ---
[13:10] Speaker 3: (inaudible)
[13:12] Jenna: Sorry, can you repeat that?
[13:15] Priya: I was asking about price predictability. If we commit, can Redwood guarantee unit pricing on the invoice?
[13:21] Jenna: Yes, committed plans fix unit pricing for the term and provide dedicated capacity guarantees. We can include burn protection clauses to avoid surprises.

--- Benchmarks and data sharing ---
[14:00] Marco: We'll share a benchmark checklist: sample prompts, 95/50/median lengths, concurrency patterns, and any critical flows that cannot tolerate >100ms added latency. Also an example spreadsheet to simulate token burn under multiple scenarios.
[14:15] Priya: Please include how you account for system tokens (e.g., system prompts, instruction tokens) vs model generation. We need that split.
[14:22] Marco: Yes, cost breakdown is per-token with categories: prompt tokens, generation tokens, cached tokens, internal overhead. We'll provide the exported CSV post-run.

--- Pricing nuance ---
[15:00] Priya: Do you charge for cached tokens?
[15:03] Jenna: Typically cached tokens reduce billed compute; however storage for cache in Dedicated/Private is part of the subscription. For Hosted, you pay for served tokens but cached hits are billed less since compute is lower; we'll show exact math in the template.
[15:18] Marcus: Any egress costs if we use Private with cross-region traffic?
[15:21] Marco: Egress depends on your cloud setup; Redwood doesn't add egress costs but Dedicated/Private architectures may require cross-region replication which could add cloud egress. We'll call that out in the cost model.

--- Timeline and decision criteria ---
[16:00] Elena: Our decision criteria: 1) keep avg latency <250ms for critical flows, 2) fit in Q4 budget of $150k (or justify headcount ops shift), 3) SOC2 and CMK support.
[16:12] Jenna: We'll map all three to pilot success metrics.

--- Recap & next steps ---
[50:00] Jenna: Quick recap: Redwood to send cost model + FastPath checklist (Marco to include batching/quant profiles). Cascade to provide sample prompts and 7-day profile. Schedule pilot kickoff week of 8/31. Jenna to share Dedicated pricing tiers and commitment discounts.
[50:23] Priya: That works. Also request an internal note for legal on HIPAA/Baa considerations.
[50:30] Marcus: We'll aim to get the logs and prompt set by 8/25.
[50:35] Elena: Looking forward to the benchmark.
[50:40] Jenna: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invite and links to the checklist and cost template.

Meeting end: 16:22 PDT

References mentioned: cost model template (link shared in chat), FastPath benchmark checklist (will be emailed), Redwood Dedicated pricing doc (sales portal link).

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K V cache" spelled out), filler words and overlaps present, speaker labels are best-effort.
